_comment: Judge-step verdicts (architecture 10.1 step 4). A reference-compare item can ONLY pass by an entry here, written by an agent that opened both images. Every entry must cite the render it judged and the round. Removing the render, or replacing it with a different file, invalidates the verdict because the runner compares the recorded byte size.

R-lantern.basis: Measured against design-reference/refs/lantern-topdown.png. Fin span 1.57x fuselage width vs reference 1.57x; head assembly 0.570x vs 0.565x; neck 0.547x vs 0.542x; lens-to-hull gap 0.77 lens radii vs 0.75. Silhouette, livery, nosecone, capsule profile, gunmetal emitter, three focusing rings, nozzle and fin star all match. D89's emitter reads as engineered tech, not a headlight. Re-judged at round 4 after an incidental re-render (165037 -> 167607 bytes, same art); ship geometry unchanged and still matching.
R-lantern.residual: Exhaust flame is a sharp hollow chevron where the reference is a solid soft-edged tapering cone. Logged as a follow-up fix task, not a blocker: it is a 20-line change in one function and does not affect the ship silhouette the item exists to check.

R-shadow.basis: Measured against design-reference/refs/shadow-sheet.png. Round 1's three findings are all closed: eyes are now large rounded pills filling the plate, the plate spans most of the head inside its cream rim, and the body is a lifted charcoal with a rim highlight rather than flat near-black. Ear pods enlarged with their blue ring, arms chunkier and angled out, raised arms drawn in front so gestures read. All six poses present and correct (idle, pointing, cheering, worried, asleep, saluting), rendered large on transparency. Bottom-row colourways correctly unused - Shadow has one look (D91). Re-judged at round 3 after a 2.1% re-render: the ear pods and flank port are now muted to match the reference, which closes the round-2 residual. Re-judged at round 4: art unchanged. The 3.1% drift is ANIMATION PHASE, not a redraw - the glow pulse and hover bob are now driven from the scene clock, so each capture samples a different frame.
R-shadow.residual: The evidence capture is not deterministic: an animated subject samples a different frame each run, so this verdict will go stale on every re-render regardless of whether the art changed. Fix is to pin the animation phase for the reference capture, not to widen the tolerance.
